title: Hierarchical queue-gating with evidence-aware truncation playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a hierarchical queue-gating system for tenant-aware admission control that pairs an SLA-escrow credit model with an evidence-aware truncation strategy for partial responses. The goal is to keep P99 latency and success SLOs within targets during multi-region spikes by combining: 1) multi-level priority queues (global -> region -> tenant), 2) timeboxed admission windows and SLA escrow credits, 3) a lightweight evidence-scoring micro-model to drive safe truncation of token sequences, and 4) circuit breaker hooks for region failover and downstream degradation policies. This playbook documents design choices, rollout plan, metrics, tests, and operators play actions.
acceptance_criteria: Priority enqueue/dequeue semantics implemented for global/region/tenant lanes with hierarchical backpressure (no cross-tenant starvation intended)
SLA escrow meter tracks credits per tenant and enforces admission caps when credits depleted; credits replenish on configured cadence
design_decisions: Hierarchical model: requests are first classified into one of three priority bands (critical, standard, best-effort) using headers + token budget hints from client; band determines lane admission order and preemption knobs

SLA escrow: tenants pre-commit credits (time-weighted) that are consumed on admission rather than on completion to avoid runaway backlog. Credits can be loaned across lanes with bounded debt windows and operator visibility

Evidence-aware truncation: deploy a 15MB micro-model (frozen, quantized) co-located with fronting routers that scores token positional importance using TF-IDF+attention-proxy features. Truncation removes low-evidence tail segments before admission to downstream GPUs to reduce p99 tail loads while preserving answer fidelity

Timebox admission windows: every request carries a soft deadline; when deadlines are tight, admission flow applies progressive degradation policies in sequence: 1) shorten context via evidence truncation, 2) switch to a cached prefix/resume path, 3) route to cheaper model variant, 4) return partial/structured response with explicit fidelity flag

Circuit breaker integration: admission gates expose a single boolean health signal per region and per model variant. If tripped, gates move affected tenants to fallback lanes and trigger multi-region reroute protocols
State visibility: all gate state, escrow balances, and truncation decisions are emitted into Console metrics and trace spans for SLO post-mortem and automated rollback decisions
implementation_notes: Router changes: extend request context with (lane_id, escrow_tokens_reserved, evidence_score, soft_deadline_ms)
Admission controller: new component implemented in Go; evaluates hierarchical quotas atomically and reserves escrow tokens using compare-and-swap to avoid double booking
Truncation service: lightweight Rust service with CPU-optimized tokenizers and a hotpath for short contexts (<1024 tokens); models run quantized and pinned to NUMA nodes
Fallbacks: cheaper model variants must be API-compatible; add a compatibility shim to map structured tool calls if variants differ in function-calling semantics
Telemetry: introduce shed_rate, escrow_depletion_events, truncation_rate, average_tokens_trimmed, and partial_response_fraction metrics; tag by region, tenant, and model
test_plan: Unit: fuzz evidence scorer with adversarial token distributions and verify deterministic trimming thresholds
Integration: synthetic traffic generator that spawns multi-region spike scenarios while varying tenant credit mixes and priority band composition
Chaos: kill region routers and validate circuit-breaker transitions and cross-region replay without double-processing requests
Perf: measure p50/p95/p99 before/after truncation and under varying batch sizes to ensure no regression in throughput
Canary: rolling canary using 3% of traffic with a shadow path that records truncation decisions and fidelity user feedback metric
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): bench evidence-aware truncation on observed production prompts; tune scoring thresholds
Phase 1 (canary): enable hierarchical gating and truncation for internal tenants + 3% production traffic; no-circuit-breaker mode (observe-only)
Phase 2 (limited): enable admission caps for best-effort band in two non-critical regions, activate circuit-breaker hooks for one model variant
Phase 3 (gradual): expand to 30% traffic across regions with operator dashboards and automatic rollback rules based on SLO breach signals
Phase 4 (full): global enable, monitor for 72h, then mark runtime-1.22 release and update runbooks
metrics: shed_rate by tenant_band (target < 0.5% for high-priority tenants)
truncation_rate and average_tokens_trimmed (used for fidelity regressions)
escrow_depletion_events per 1k requests (used to tune credit replenishment)
